LESSON: UTENSILS USED AT HOME

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Home
Topic 3.1: Utensils used at home
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Utensils used at home, part of My Home in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have utensils at home?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Utensils used at home together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity: as learner model or colour utensils used at home.

• Communication and Collaboration: learner uses appropriate expression and gestures when singing songs about utensils used at home.

• Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices with assistive technology to watch\listen to audio clips on utensils used at home.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner properly handles utensils used at home.

• Unity: learner enhances cooperation when sharing pictures of utensils found at home.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
17

Safety: learner develops responsibility for self when handling utensils found at home

Link to other learning areas:

Utensils used at home relates to concepts of sorting and grouping objects according to size in Mathematical Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards, tactile diagrams, flash cards, photos, drawn pictures, crayons, pencils, clay, plasticine, realia (plates, cups, spoons), braille

writing materials and equipment.
